function: Learned deep-autoencoder state-space model drives an MPC that sets the uplink transmit power of NOMA IoT devices to track target SINR and rate (pp. 2-5).
system: Direct-to-satellite IoT uplink, NOMA; 480-satellite LEO constellation; 6 or 12 devices; 868 MHz; antenna gains 5 dBi (device), 30 dBi (satellite); no RIS (pp. 2, 6).
method: Deep autoencoder and feedforward networks learn a state-space model of power-to-SINR dynamics, whose matrices drive an MPC; supervised, simulated data (pp. 3-4).
data_channel: Own simulator: free-space loss plus Rician fading with elevation-dependent K-factor; 12 days of LEO trajectories at 1 s, 1,036,806 rows; simulated only (pp. 2-4).
test_conditions: 70/15/15 train/test/validation split of simulated data from six devices; five closed-loop cases, Case 5 with 12 devices; retraining not stated (pp. 4, 6).
baselines: Only DAE-LQR, a deep-autoencoder LQR controller [28]; no classical power-allocation method and no earlier learned power-allocation method (p. 7).
metrics: SINR tracking and settling time, transmission rate, allocated power, energy in mWh, regression R of the neural model (pp. 4, 6-7).
complexity: none; only a qualitative remark that DAE-LQR has lower execution time and memory use, details deferred to the Appendix (p. 7).
openness: none; only supplementary material at the article DOI, described as the Appendix, with no code or data stated (pp. 1, 7).
q1_support: p. 2: "the uplink channel can be modeled using a Rician distribution". Not met: own free-space plus Rician model with simulated data (p. 4: "Simulated data are used because real-time data is not available for the DtSIoT scenario"); 3GPP TR 38.811 is cited only to name the DtSIoT configurations (p. 1).
q2_support: p. 4: "The data sets are segmented into three parts with ratios of 70%, 15%, and 15% for training, testing, and validation purposes." Not met: only a split of the same simulated data (six devices); p. 6: "the DAE-MPC controller is evaluated on a larger-scale scenario featuring 12 IoT devices", but the paper does not say whether the model was retrained or reused.
q3_support: p. 7: "compared with a Deep Autoencoder-based Linear Quadratic Regulator (DAE-LQR) [28]". Not met: DAE-LQR is a deep-autoencoder controller of the same family with LQR in place of MPC, and [28] (p. 8) is a classical PID/LQR paper on an inverted pendulum, so there is no non-learned power-allocation baseline and no earlier learned one.
q4_support: p. 7: "offers better computational efficiency (lower execution time and memory usage)". Not met: the remark is qualitative; no complexity order, operation count, parameter count or runtime is given, and the details are deferred to the Appendix, which is not in the PDF.
q5_support: p. 4: "Simulated data are used because real-time data is not available for the DtSIoT scenario". Not met: no code or dataset is released; p. 1 cites only "supplementary downloadable material available at https://doi.org/10.1109/JIOT.2025.3578093", which the text describes as the Appendix (literature, theorems, DAE-LQR details).
notes: Included as area 6: power control of a LEO direct-to-satellite NOMA uplink. Borderline for no_learning: the learned element is the deep-autoencoder state-space model inside a classical MPC, kept because the controller is built from the learned model (pp. 2-5). The Appendix and supplementary material are not in the PDF, so the DAE-LQR details, any complexity figures and any released files could not be checked; q4 and q5 rest on the main text only. Case 5 uses 12 devices while the training data has six (Table I, p. 4), with no statement on retraining, so q2 is 0.
